claim: The llm-d EPP defines a general EndpointDiscovery plugin interface located at pkg/epp/framework/interface/datalayer/discovery.go that separates endpoint enumeration from routing logic.
stance_target: llm-d router can be extended to support non-Kubernetes backends via a plugin interface
scope_conditions: llm-d router / EPP codebase, as of the blog post accompanying/around v0.9 (referenced alongside 'llm-d 0.9 is here' banner)
quoted_support: The llm-d EPP now defines a general `EndpointDiscovery` plugin interface: anything that can enumerate endpoints and stream upsert/delete events satisfies it - a file on disk, Consul, etcd, a cloud provider's service-discovery API, or the Kubernetes watch itself.

claim: The EndpointDiscovery Go interface requires Start(ctx, notifier) error and Ready() <-chan struct{}; DiscoveryNotifier requires Upsert(endpoint *EndpointMetadata) and Delete(id types.NamespacedName).
stance_target: exact API shape of EndpointDiscovery plugin interface
scope_conditions: llm-d-router repo, file pkg/epp/framework/interface/datalayer/discovery.go, main branch, as quoted in blog dated around llm-d v0.9 (2026)
quoted_support: type EndpointDiscovery interface{ fwkplugin.Plugin; Start(ctx context.Context, notifier DiscoveryNotifier) error; Ready() <-chan struct{} }

claim: The FileDiscovery plugin reads a YAML/JSON file of endpoints and optionally watches it via fsnotify, requiring each entry to have a unique name and literal address:port (hostnames not resolved), with optional labels such as llm-d.ai/role: prefill exposed to scheduler plugins.
stance_target: file-based discovery is a viable, documented non-Kubernetes backend for the llm-d router
scope_conditions: llm-d no-Kubernetes deployment mode, as of blog post ~2026
quoted_support: Each entry needs a unique `name` and a literal `address:port` (hostnames are not resolved); optional `labels` are surfaced to scheduler plugins, e.g. `llm-d.ai/role: prefill` for P/D.

claim: Switching an EPP from Kubernetes discovery to file discovery requires only one config line: dataLayer.discovery.pluginRef: file-discovery in the EndpointPickerConfig, after registering the file-discovery plugin.
stance_target: customizing the router's backend discovery is a low-effort, config-level change once a plugin exists
scope_conditions: llm-d EPP config schema as of blog post ~2026
quoted_support: Turning a Kubernetes EPP into a no-Kubernetes EPP comes down to a single line in the `EndpointPickerConfig`: after registering the file-discovery plugin, point discovery at it with `dataLayer.discovery.pluginRef: file-discovery`.

claim: Two features still require Kubernetes CRDs even off-cluster: per-request priority via InferenceObjective, and model-name rewriting via InferenceModelRewrite; both fall back to static config or are unavailable outside Kubernetes.
stance_target: non-Kubernetes llm-d router deployment has full feature parity with Kubernetes deployment
scope_conditions: llm-d router file-discovery mode as of blog post ~2026; stated as a known limitation, with a stated plan to move these behind the same plugin pattern
quoted_support: A few features are still configured through Kubernetes CRDs - per-request priority from `InferenceObjective`, and `InferenceModelRewrite`-driven model-name rewriting - so outside Kubernetes they fall back to static configuration or are not yet available; the plan is to move them behind the same plugin pattern as discovery.

claim: Off Kubernetes, endpoint lifecycle removal (detecting a dead worker and removing it) is not automatic; it is the surrounding orchestrator's (Ray, Slurm, custom controller) responsibility, typically via a small health-monitoring agent that rewrites the endpoints file.
stance_target: file discovery mode automatically detects and evicts failed endpoints the way Kubernetes InferencePool does
scope_conditions: llm-d file-discovery mode, as of blog post ~2026
quoted_support: on Kubernetes a dying pod leaves the `InferencePool` automatically, while with file discovery detecting a failed worker and rewriting the file is the surrounding orchestrator's job (Ray, Slurm, a custom controller) - in production usually a small health-monitoring agent that drops unavailable workers from the file.

claim: Future/planned EndpointDiscovery plugins named explicitly by the llm-d team include SlurmDiscovery and RayDiscovery for orchestrator-native discovery with no file in the loop, plus service-registry-backed plugins (Consul, etcd, cloud provider service discovery), and eventual migration of the existing Kubernetes watch behind the same interface.
stance_target: roadmap for additional non-Kubernetes backend plugins beyond file discovery
scope_conditions: stated as 'future work' / 'exploring' in blog post ~2026, not yet merged
quoted_support: Orchestrator-native discovery plugin (future work) - for the most dynamic case, a dedicated `SlurmDiscovery` or `RayDiscovery` plugin against the same `EndpointDiscovery` interface, talking to the orchestrator directly with no file in the loop.

claim: Prefill/decode disaggregation works unchanged in file-discovery mode; the only file-discovery-specific change is marking each endpoint's role via the llm-d.ai/role label (prefill or decode), with the full set of role values defined in pkg/epp/framework/plugins/scheduling/filter/bylabel/roles.go.
stance_target: advanced llm-d routing features (P/D disaggregation) are preserved when swapping in a custom discovery backend
scope_conditions: llm-d-router repo, file bylabel/roles.go, as of blog post ~2026
quoted_support: The only file-discovery-specific change is marking each endpoint's role in the YAML with the `llm-d.ai/role` label (`prefill` or `decode`); the router's prefill/decode filters select candidates by that label.

claim: The existing Kubernetes InferencePool watch is planned to be refactored to sit behind the same EndpointDiscovery interface as file/DNS/service-registry discovery, so Kubernetes support becomes just another plugin rather than a special case.
stance_target: the architecture is designed for symmetry across backends, not Kubernetes-as-default plus a bolt-on
scope_conditions: stated design intent as of blog post ~2026; not yet implemented per the text ('is expected to move')
quoted_support: The existing Kubernetes watch is expected to move behind this same interface, so that `InferencePool` discovery becomes just another plugin alongside file, DNS, and service-registry discovery.

claim: SemiAnalysis's InferenceX benchmark framework runs on native Slurm with no Kubernetes, and llm-d's no-Kubernetes mode is what allowed llm-d to be integrated into it.
stance_target: non-Kubernetes llm-d has real external adoption for benchmarking
quoted_support: SemiAnalysis's [InferenceX](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX) benchmark framework is a concrete example: it runs on native Slurm with no Kubernetes, and llm-d's no-Kubernetes mode is what let llm-d be integrated into it.
